_comment: The living world's economy (scripts/sim/world_economy.gd WorldEconomy; DESIGN_LIVING_WORLD.md M1). Built from data/countries.json, data/cities.json and data/production.json. Markets are trade zones (a country, or a big country's coastline zone, with its ports); each has a stockpile and a price per good. Every calendar day each zone makes what its plants make, its pops and industry use what they need, and ships' arrivals and departures move stock. A good's price follows its days of cover (stockpile / daily use) against cover_days: base x (cover_days / cover) ^ price_power, capped to price_range, x the country's currency strength x the port's local factor.
_units_comment: Turning the real 2016 units of production.json into the game's units (markets.json unit): crate_t (a seafood crate in tonnes), pallet_t (a produce pallet), timber_t_per_m3; grades: the metal share of each ore as shipped (concentrate), so ore tonnes = metal tonnes / grade; container_totals: the world's yearly output, in containers, of the goods production.json gives as shares (manufactured goods).
_prices_comment: cover_days: the days of use a zone's stockpile normally holds (at that cover, the base price); price_power: how hard price answers cover; price_range: [cheapest, dearest] x base; start_cover: [least, most] days a zone starts with (more for one that makes the good, less for one that only uses it); port_spread: a port's local factor runs from 1 - port_spread (the zone's biggest port) to 1 + port_spread (its smallest); demand_power: how much a good's use falls as its price rises (price ^ -demand_power); substitution: how strongly pops switch within a need to the cheaper goods; supply_power: how much plants' output answers price (from supply_floor of capacity at the cheapest).
_strata_comment: A place's people split into lower, middle and upper strata by its country's GDP a head (US$): middle = middle_min + (middle_max - middle_min) x the wealth (0 at poor_gdp, 1 at rich_gdp, on a log scale), upper likewise; the rest lower. Cities lean richer: in a port metro or inland city the middle and upper shares are x city_lean, in the countryside x rural_lean (renormalized). wealth_power: how much a country's wealth (its GDP a head against world_gdp_per_head) lifts every stratum's spending.
_needs_comment: What pops buy: each need's goods (any of them satisfies it; the cheapest mix is bought first) and how much a person of each stratum wants of it ([lower, middle, upper]; relative weights, the world's output of each good is shared out by them). Goods no need lists are used by industry (users).
_users_comment: Who else uses each good, and how much of its world output: [[driver, share]...]. Drivers: make:<good> (a zone uses it in proportion to what it makes of that good), gdp (by the zone's GDP), people (by its population), farming (by its crops). A good in a need and here splits its world output between them by these shares (the need's part shared by people, the rest by these drivers). @cars, @trucks, @boats: every maker of that kind.
_people_comment: How people move: growth is each country's real 2016 yearly growth, x (1 + living_growth x (its standard of living - 1)) so a better-off zone grows a little faster; migration moves migration_share a year of a country's rural people into its cities.
_currency_comment: A country's currency strength drifts with its trade balance: by rate a year x (exports - imports) / (exports + imports) by value over about the last balance_days, held within range.
